correctness.rationale: For every prime-power q and d>=2, total domination of the full point--affine-hyperplane incidence graph splits exactly into a point set meeting every hyperplane and a hyperplane family covering every point. Brouwer--Schrijver sharp blocking lower bound is d(q-1)+1; cardinality counting gives at least q covering hyperplanes. Coordinate-axis points B={0} union {c e_i:c !=0} hit every hyperplane and parallel x1=c planes cover all points, attaining d(q-1)+q+1. A perfect matching in the selected bipartite subgraph demands equal selected counts, hence paired size >=2d(q-1)+2; the explicit x_i=c nonzero planes plus x1=0 match the same B bijectively and cover all points. Reconstructed definitions, q=2/d=2 and q=3/d=2 exact independent incidence enumeration yields total/paired (5,6) and (8,10). No extrapolation from these finite cases is needed for the infinite family; non-Desarguesian geometries excluded.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Brouwer--Schrijver covers the point-blocking subproblem (used and credited), while Héger--Nagy treats ordinary dominating sets in projective incidence graphs and Adriaensen--Mattheus--Spiro edge domination/minimal maximal matchings. Neither strengthens to the submitted two full affine vertex-domination minima.

value.rationale: The canonical incidence graphs of all finite affine spaces exhibit a sharp, unbounded penalty (d-1)(q-1) for requiring matched back-up protection; the independent blocking, covering and perfect-matching obstructions make a structural graph-theoretic phenomenon rather than a tiny numerical instance. Both exact finite-field parameter optima and constructive witnesses are useful benchmarks. The classical blocking bound itself is acknowledged as prior.

limitations: Prime powers and d>=2 only; does not classify all optimizers or general affine planes.
